lessons.title: Composition tree and execution DAG are different truths
lessons.statement: Use a tree for incremental Agent composition and a DAG for executable dependencies, fan-out, fan-in, and reruns.
avoid: treating parent-child hierarchy as execution order

lessons.title: Roles are views, not kernel stages
lessons.statement: PM, Developer, Tester, Researcher, Release, and Marketing should compose reusable capabilities without acquiring mandatory sequencing authority.
applies_when: adding a new department or role
avoid: one expensive Agent call per role

lessons.title: Cheap executors need bounded tasks, not the whole project conversation
lessons.statement: Send each executor only its node goal, declared inputs, relevant direct dependencies, constraints, context, and acceptance condition.

lessons.title: Functional proof precedes scale proof
lessons.statement: One real project that composes, executes, tests, repairs locally, and finishes is more valuable than large DAG, concurrency, latency, or soak results before the substrate works.
avoid: stress tests as a substitute for product function

lessons.title: Archive before physical deletion during authority migration
lessons.statement: Move superseded source, tests, schemas, and documents together under a clearly non-active legacy path before later deletion, while Git history remains the final archive.
avoid: leaving active tests for removed modules

lessons.title: Self-growth is validated capability acquisition
lessons.statement: A capability gap should trigger search, bounded trial, interface adaptation, tests, registry admission, and reuse; it should not trigger unrestricted kernel rewriting.

lessons.title: Repository and product evidence are separate
lessons.statement: A commit, remote SHA, or CI pass proves repository state only; it does not prove that a real project was generated, executed, or accepted.
avoid: raising product level from test count
